subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw repair already-persisted same-parent compaction retry forks by dropping provable dead-end compaction entries, or only prevent new forks at the compaction writer/retry layer?
rationale: This choice rewrites or preserves persisted session history, and repository policy treats session state and repair/migration behavior as compatibility-sensitive maintainer-owned decisions.

options.title: Repair existing forks narrowly
options.body: Accept a constrained repair that drops only compaction-vs-compaction dead-end siblings with tests proving legitimate branches are preserved.

options.title: Prevent only future forks
options.body: Fix compaction retry idempotency or deterministic event identity and leave already-corrupted JSONL sessions for manual recovery or a later doctor migration.

options.title: Pause for broader session-tree policy
options.body: Hold the linked PR until maintainers choose a general invariant for compaction, leaf records, and concurrent branch reconstruction.

recommendation.title: Repair existing forks narrowly
recommendation.body: Accept a constrained repair that drops only compaction-vs-compaction dead-end siblings with tests proving legitimate branches are preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a maintainer-level session-state compatibility decision, and the current release/session repair history points to vincentkoc as the strongest available routing owner.
